Subject: Vendor economics comparison & on-ramp request

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked promising. Procurement asked me to get a formal commercial comparison versus our incumbent (CloudLayer) and to understand what kind of on-ramp economics Redwood can offer if we move forward.

Can you send a side-by-side 12-month TCO (including expected token/unit costs, committed discounts, typical integration/onboarding effort in person/weeks, and any migration credits)? BrightBasket is evaluating replacement cost + ramp risk; our decision window is Dec 15.

A few quick facts to help you model: current committed spend ~ $40k/month (approx $480k ARR), peak sustained QPS ~ 120 (US-East), 95th latency target ~ 120ms, and we require SOC2 + basic EU data residency for one business line (but majority is US).

Procurement will want a price-match on key line items. Specifically they asked: (1) can you match the effective per-token economics if we migrate, (2) what migration/onboarding credit do you provide, and (3) do you offer a short, low-cost pilot to validate quality before committing?

If you can send me a short commercial packet (one pager + spreadsheet) by end of day Mon Nov 30 that'd be ideal.

Appreciate it — Charlie

Charlie Moore

Talk soon,

Subject: Fwd: Vendor economics comparison & on-ramp request — quick commercial options (internal)

Forwarding Charlie's ask. Decision window: Dec 15. BrightBasket current spend ~ $40k/mo; target: price-match CloudLayer on effective per-unit cost and ask for migration credits.

My proposed options to present (draft):

Option 1 — Pilot On-ramp (low risk):
- 3-month pilot: up to $15k in committed usage (no charge for overage first 30 days)
- Migration: 2-week migration sprint (solutions hours), plus $12k onboarding credit against the first invoice
- No long-term commitment; then month-to-month pricing with 10% recommended discount if converted within 90 days

Option 2 — Committed Starter (preferred for conversion):
- 12-month committed term @ 18% discount off list usage rates (applies to committed volume only)
- Onboarding credit: $25k applied up-front to offset migration and integration costs
- 60 days of dedicated migration support (includes 2 onsite or equivalent remote weeks)
- SLA credit/penalty clause for p95 latency miss on provisioned throughput

Asks for Finance/RevOps: (Connor) please provide margin impact for both options and a firm floor for %-discount and credit sizes.
(Connor: what are you comfortable approving vs what needs RevOps/legal?)

Connor — please see inline reply below.

— Aisha

--- Connor's inline reply ---
From: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:26:00 -0800

Aisha — thanks. Margin quick calc (back-of-envelope):
- Option 1: Onboarding credit $12k + lost mgmt ops (~$8k) => ~ $20k one-time cost; very low lifetime guarantee so not material for <6 months but higher churn risk.
- Option 2: $25k credit + 18% margin hit on committed volume -> estimated ARR impact ~ $70k over 12 months (given $480k baseline) before factoring retention upside.

Approval thresholds: I can sign off up to $30k one-time credits and up to 20% discount on committed usage for a named account. Anything larger needs RevOps and Sales Leadership sign-off. For this account, Option 2 looks acceptable if we secure a minimum 9-month commit or guarantee on renewal. Also recommend a SKU bundling: separate a premium low-latency route (higher price) for the B2C BU that needs EU residency.

I'll attach a sample cost worksheet and a DocuSign envelope template for standard SOW flow.

— Connor

--- Monica's inline reply ---
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:35:00 -0800

Aisha / Connor — ops note: the 2-week sprint estimate is realistic but we should budget an extra week for verification and runbook handoff. I'm fine offering the two-week onsite equivalent plus an extra week of remote validation as a standard inclusion for Option 2. That reduces the effective onboarding credit we need to hand out.

— Monica
